intro:
Profound is one of the best-known names in AI visibility tracking (often called AEO or GEO) — monitoring whether ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI and other engines mention and recommend your brand. The product is real and the data is respected. The honest question for a small business isn't "is Profound good?" but "is it the right fit for *me*, at *this* price, *before* I've seen any value?"

That's where it gets harder. Profound is built and priced for larger organizations, and its buying process asks you to commit before you can see whether AI engines even recommend you. Below is a fair look at the cost, what you actually get at each tier, and how to test your AI visibility for free before spending a cent.

sections.heading: The short version: it's enterprise software at an enterprise price
sections.body:
Profound is openly positioned for mid-market and enterprise brands — companies with dedicated marketing teams and meaningful budgets. That's not a knock; it's a deliberate strategy, and the platform is built well for that audience.

The practical consequence for a small business is cost and commitment. There's no free trial and no free self-serve tier. Public pricing references a $99/month Starter plan and a roughly $399/month Growth plan, while the official pricing page now leans heavily on customized enterprise pricing — meaning the full picture often runs through a sales conversation. If your total AEO budget is under a couple thousand dollars a month, you're likely not the customer Profound was designed for. None of that makes Profound bad. It makes it a mismatch for most solo founders, early-stage startups, and small agencies who need to prove value before they can defend the spend.

sections.heading: What you actually get at each tier
sections.body:
This is the part reviewers flag most often. The entry plan looks affordable, but the capability you probably want sits higher up:

- **Starter (~$99/mo):** Widely described as effectively a ChatGPT-only demo — limited prompts, a single engine. Useful as a taste, not as real multi-engine monitoring.
- **Growth (~$399/mo):** Where ongoing tracking across a few answer engines actually begins. This is the realistic starting point for meaningful use, not $99.
- **Enterprise (custom):** Full multi-engine coverage, API access, longer history, SSO and higher limits — priced through a custom contract.

So the headline price and the useful price are far apart. For a small team, that gap is the crux of the problem: you're often comparing your needs against the $399+ reality, not the $99 sticker. Always confirm exact engine coverage and prompt limits for your specific plan before assuming a tier does what you need — the depth that makes Profound impressive lives in the heavier plans.

sections.heading: The real friction: you commit before you see value
sections.body:
The structural issue for a small buyer is the order of operations. Profound is sales-led: for full coverage you book a demo and move toward a contract *before* you can see whether AI engines actually recommend your brand. There's no free, instant way to look first.

For an enterprise with a procurement process and a marketing team, that's normal and fine. For a small business owner or a lean agency, it's backwards. You're being asked to invest time in a sales call and budget in a subscription to answer a question — "do AI engines recommend me, and who's winning instead?" — that you'd really like a quick, honest answer to *before* deciding anything. Reviewers consistently cite this as the hardest part to justify for small teams: the cost and commitment come before the proof.

sections.heading: When Profound genuinely is worth it
sections.body:
To be fair, there are real cases where Profound earns its price:

- You're a mid-market or enterprise brand with a dedicated marketing or SEO team.
- AI search is a strategic channel and you have budget allocated to it (think four figures a month and up).
- You need depth: detailed analytics, historical dashboards, larger prompt volumes, API access, and enterprise controls like SSO.
- You want a vendor with a sales and support relationship, and a procurement process that's comfortable with custom contracts.

If that's you, Profound's maturity and analytics depth are a genuine strength, and the enterprise motion is a feature, not a bug. The mismatch is specifically with *small* businesses — solo operators, early-stage startups, and small agencies — who need to validate the channel cheaply before scaling spend. For them, the price-to-proof ratio is the problem, not the product quality.

sections.heading: A free way to test your AI visibility first
sections.body:
Before you book any demo or sign any contract, it's worth simply *seeing* where you stand. That's exactly the gap AEOeye fills.

It's blind, multi-engine querying you can run yourself.

Being equally honest: AEOeye is newer and lighter than Profound on enterprise analytics and long-term historical dashboards, and its deeper multi-engine tracking builds up with ongoing use. If the results show this channel matters to you and you outgrow a lightweight tool, *then* evaluate whether a heavier platform like Profound is worth the enterprise commitment — now with real data in hand instead of a leap of faith.

faqs.q: Does Profound have a free trial?
faqs.a: No. Profound has no free trial and no free self-serve tier. For full multi-engine coverage you book a demo and move toward a paid contract before you can see whether AI engines recommend your brand. If you want to look first for free, AEOeye runs an instant AI visibility audit across ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI, Claude and Gemini with no sales call required.

faqs.q: How much does Profound actually cost?
faqs.a: Public sources reference a Starter plan around $99/month and a Growth plan around $399/month, with full coverage on a custom Enterprise contract. The catch is that the $99 tier is widely described as a ChatGPT-only demo, so meaningful, ongoing multi-engine tracking realistically starts around $399/month. Always confirm current pricing and exact engine coverage with Profound directly.

faqs.q: Is Profound good for a small business or solo founder?
faqs.a: For most small businesses it's hard to justify. Profound is built and priced for mid-market and enterprise teams with dedicated marketing staff and budget. If your AEO budget is under roughly a couple thousand dollars a month, you're likely not the intended customer. It's worth it once AI search is a strategic, funded channel — and far less so when you're just trying to validate whether it matters.

faqs.q: What's a good free alternative to test AI visibility before paying?
faqs.a: AEOeye gives you a free, instant audit across ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI, Claude and Gemini — showing whether engines recommend you, where you rank, and which competitors win, with no sales call or contract. It's lighter than Profound on enterprise analytics and historical dashboards, so it's best as a fast way to see whether you have an AI visibility problem before deciding whether a heavier platform is worth it.

faqs.q: Why does Profound require a sales call instead of letting me sign up?
faqs.a: Profound is a sales-led enterprise platform, so its full product runs through a demo and a custom contract rather than instant self-serve signup. That model suits large organizations with procurement processes, but it means small buyers commit time and budget before seeing results — which is the main reason it's a poor fit for lean teams that need to prove value quickly.
